name: Superpowers
tagline: A set of rules that teach your AI coding assistant to plan first, test everything and debug carefully - like a senior engineer would.
sentence: Install 15 skills into your coding tool and it stops rushing into code - it asks questions, writes a plan, builds tests before features, reviews its own work and catches mistakes before you see them.

board.say: AI coding assistants rush straight into writing code - they skip planning, ignore edge cases, forget to write tests and produce sloppy work that breaks later.
You install the skills once and they activate automatically every time you start a coding task.
Your coding project - any codebase you're working on with an AI assistant.
The skills change how the AI assistant approaches every task - planning, building, testing and reviewing.
steps: Before coding, the assistant asks clarifying questions and drafts a design for your approval
It writes a detailed plan, then works through it using test-driven development - tests first, code second
When the code is done, it runs its own code review, catches issues, and only marks the task complete after verifying everything works

board.say: An AI assistant that works like a careful senior engineer instead of a rushed intern.

outputs.what: A structured plan before any code
outputs.eg: The assistant writes a plan document with acceptance criteria, then asks you to approve it before starting
For a new feature, it writes the test cases first, confirms they fail, then writes the code to make them pass
Before marking a task done, the assistant reviews its own changes, checks for edge cases and runs the test suite

before: Your AI assistant dives straight into writing code without asking what you actually want
It produces code that works for the obvious case but breaks on edge cases nobody tested
You spend time reviewing and fixing mistakes the assistant should have caught itself
after: The assistant asks questions first, writes a plan, and waits for your approval before coding
Tests are written before features - the assistant proves the code works, not just that it compiles
A self-review step catches common mistakes before you ever see the code
uses_note: Superpowers has 309K stars and 3.6M installs on skills.sh. The creator says the assistant can 'sometimes work autonomously for a couple of hours without deviating from the plan,' but independent benchmarks are thin.

steps: In Claude Code, run `/plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official`. For other tools, see the [install guide](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) - there are one-line installs for 16 AI coding tools.
Start a new session and give it a task - for example, 'Let's make a React to-do list.' The assistant should start by asking clarifying questions instead of jumping into code.
Follow the assistant's plan - it will write tests first, then code, then review its own work before marking the task done.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/obra/superpowers
Then: Install the skills and test with a small coding task - the assistant should brainstorm and plan before writing any code.

footprint.disk: The skills are plain text files - the entire repo is well under 1 MB.
footprint.memory: No runtime memory - the skills are instructions loaded into the AI assistant's context window.
footprint.runs_on: Works with 16 AI coding tools: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex (app and CLI), Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Grok Build CLI, Kimi Code, OpenCode, and others. No operating system restriction.

best_for: Anyone using an AI coding assistant who wants more reliable, better-tested output
Teams that want their AI tools to follow a consistent development process
People new to AI-assisted coding who want guardrails on the assistant's behavior
skip_if: You prefer to control the process yourself and find pre-set workflows restrictive
You use AI for quick one-off scripts where planning overhead isn't worth it
Your team already has strict coding standards the AI follows

alternatives.name: mattpocock/skills
alternatives.line: Matt Pocock's engineering skills - broader (55 skills) and more focused on day-to-day engineering tasks than methodology

alternatives.name: ECC
alternatives.line: A performance optimization system for coding agents - focuses on speed and efficiency rather than methodology

watch: **Very opinionated.** Superpowers enforces one specific development methodology (plan, test, review). If your team has its own process, the skills may conflict with it.
**Adds overhead to quick tasks.** The brainstorming and planning steps add time. For a one-line fix or a quick script, the ceremony can feel like overkill.
**Works best with Claude Code.** The README lists 16 tools, but the creator built and tested it primarily with Claude Code. Other tools may not trigger all skills correctly.
